data.label: Synthetic services (logs + traces)
data.description: Existing synthetic workloads instrumented with OpenTelemetry. They emit logs and distributed traces for the incident scenario. Their content is untrusted.

data.label: Telemetry collection
data.description: An OpenTelemetry Collector exports OTLP logs/spans to an Event Hubs namespace. Trace and span IDs are kept so logs and traces can be correlated. Authentication uses managed identity.

data.label: Redaction
data.description: Masks secrets, tokens, emails and IPs using reviewed rules before storage, and records a redaction audit count. Raw events aren't persisted after redaction.

data.label: Log & trace store / search
data.description: Stores the redacted logs and spans in separate tables joined on trace_id. The analysis runtime runs read-only KQL queries over time windows and services. Retention still needs to be decided.

data.label: Incident analysis runtime
data.description: Takes an operator's question and runs bounded, read-only KQL queries to correlate error spans with logs. It sends delimited evidence to the model as untrusted data, checks that every claim cites an evidence ID, and abstains if the evidence is insufficient. It does not take any actions.

data.label: Prompt-injection screening
data.description: Screens retrieved log text for injected instructions before it is sent to the model. Flagged excerpts are quarantined and shown to the operator.

data.label: LLM
data.description: Hosts the model deployment used for the incident explanation. Which model to use and its regional availability are unverified. Local tests use scripted responses instead.

data.label: Operator incident console
data.description: A web UI where operators ask about an incident and get a timeline, a probable cause and linked log/span evidence.

data.label: On-call operator
data.description: The person investigating the incident. External to provisioning.

data.label: Pipeline observability
data.description: Monitors the pipeline itself: ingestion lag, redaction failures, model latency/errors and abstentions.

brief.application: Use Azure for this synthetic architecture qualification. Correlate synthetic logs and distributed traces to explain a service incident. Include collection, redaction, storage/search, an AI analysis runtime and an operator-facing answer with source evidence. Treat log text as untrusted. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: Where do the files live, and roughly how many are there?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “SharePoint and a shared drive, about 20,000 files”.

requirements.statement: Redact secrets and personal identifiers from logs and traces before they are stored or sent to the model.
requirements.rationale: Proposed: if raw telemetry reaches storage or the LLM, credentials or personal data could leak.

requirements.statement: Treat log text as untrusted data: screen it for injected instructions, never follow instructions found inside it, and keep the analysis runtime read-only.
requirements.rationale: Log text can contain prompt injection that could mislead the explanation.

requirements.statement: Each incident explanation cites the log or span evidence behind it, and the system abstains when evidence is insufficient.
requirements.rationale: Without evidence, operators can't verify an AI-generated cause during an incident.
requirements.basis: User: "an operator-facing answer with source evidence"

decisions.subject: design.azure-log-trace-incident-analysis-first-end-to-end-sketch
decisions.title: Azure log/trace incident analysis – first end-to-end sketch
decisions.context: Scope: synthetic services' logs and distributed traces are collected (OpenTelemetry Collector → Azure Event Hubs), redacted (Azure Functions), stored/searched (Azure Data Explorer), analysed by an AI runtime (Azure Container Apps + Azure OpenAI with Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields) and returned to operators in an Entra-protected App Service web app with cited trace/log evidence. Assumptions: synthetic data only; regions are not yet selected; Azure OpenAI model and its regional availability are unverified; there's no native Terraform generator for these Azure components yet, so they're design-only and need engineering work. Nothing is deployed.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
